in_hebrew.name: אנתיאה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם אנתיאה נגזר מהמילה היוונית 'אנתוס', שפירושה פרח או תפרחת. בהקשר המקראי, השם עשוי להיות קשור לפריחה רוחנית או לפרחי הגן של ה', כפי שנזכר בספרי התנך השונים.

in_greek.name: Ανθεία
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ανθεία προέρχεται από το ελληνικό 'άνθος', που σημαίνει λουλούδι ή ανθός. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, παρόμοιοι όροι χρησιμοποιούνται για να περιγράψουν πνευματική ανάπτυξη και την ομορφιά της ψυχής.

in_latin.name: Antheia
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Antheia derivatur a verbo Graeco 'anthos', quod florem significat. In ecclesia primitiva, similia nomina adhibebantur ad describendam spiritualem crescentiam et pulchritudinem animae.

in_english.name: Antheia
in_english.meaning: Derived from Greek, meaning flower or blossom
in_english.long_meaning: The name Antheia originates from the Greek word 'anthos', meaning flower or blossom. It symbolizes spiritual growth, beauty of the soul, and flourishing faith. Though not directly mentioned in the Bible, similar names and concepts are found throughout scripture, emphasizing the importance of spiritual blossoming.

data.cultural_impact: The name Antheia carries a rich cultural impact, reminding us of the beauty and elegance found in nature, specifically flowers. It has been used in literature and mythology as a representation of grace and refinement. In ancient Greece, Antheia was a goddess associated with forests, spring, and flowers.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, Antheia represents the eternal beauty and grace found in God's creation and His divine presence. It reminds us to appreciate the simple treasures of nature and to strive for the beauty and refinement of our souls, seeking to mirror the graceful character of our Creator.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Antheia was a nymph in Greek mythology. The name Antheia carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
